text:
olivia.p: Quick help pls — had an ER visit while traveling and hospital billed under my old legal name (Olivia Park -> now Olivia Patel). Insurer denied for patient name mismatch and used my old member ID. I have both IDs and the court name-change docs on my phone. Hospital wants proof before they re-bill. What is the fastest route to get this corrected so I don't get a collections notice?

sarah.benefits: Sorry that sucks. Short path: provider should resubmit with the current subscriber name and current member ID. Since there's a name change, include a cover letter and attach a copy of the member ID plus the legal name-change document. If carrier rejected because the claim came in before their system updated, ask provider to include both old and new member IDs on the corrected claim and reference the denial EOB.

olivia.p: Hospital says EOB shows "subscriber not found" and they need an insurer contact or letter confirming coverage on the service date. Can Redwood send a verification note to the hospital?

jordan.hr: We can send a coverage verification (not a guarantee of payment) confirming active enrollment on service date and both member IDs. Send me the service date, claim number from the hospital, and a photo of both ID cards and the legal doc. I'll prepare the note and email the hospital billing contact.

benefits-bot: FYI: cross-referencing old/new member IDs accelerates reprocessing. Typical re-adjudication time 14-45 days. Mark ticket as "name-change coverage verification". If collections notice appears, escalate immediately.

olivia.p: Posting the details in DM to jordan now. Also they want a short templated line the insurer will accept if I email appeals myself. Can you paste?

sarah.benefits: Use this short appeal/verification message to send to the insurer or upload in the portal with docs: 

"To: [Insurer Provider Relations]
Member name (current): Olivia Patel (DOB: 1993-04-02)
Member name (former): Olivia Park
Member IDs: RWD-001234567 (current), RWD-000987654 (old)
Service date: 2026-03-20
Provider claim ref: HOSP-445566

Issue: Claim denied due to subscriber name/ID mismatch after a legal name change. Attached are copies of both member ID cards, legal name-change documentation, and the hospital's billed claim showing the old name. Please reprocess the claim under the current member name and ID or advise if a corrected claim from the provider is required.

Requested action: Re-adjudicate with name/ID cross-reference and issue corrected EOB if adjustment is made.

Contact: olivia.p@example.com / (555) 555-3344
"

jordan.hr: Sent the coverage verification to the hospital billing contact and cc'd benefits@redwood.com. I included both IDs, the service date, and said we will follow up with the insurer appeal if needed. Hospital acknowledged receipt and said they'll attempt re-bill, may ask for formal POA if they need someone to sign on your behalf.

olivia.p: If they ask POA, can spouse/partner sign a POA email? I'm still abroad.

jordan.hr: Partner email OK for billing POA if you sign/authorize it — have partner include your name, claim ID, and explicit line: "I, Sam Patel, am authorized by Olivia Patel to act on billing matters for claim HOSP-445566." Preferably have you email a short authorization to the hospital too (one-liner) so their compliance team is happy.

nyla.finance: If you end up paying anything to stop immediate collections, save receipts and the corrected EOB. Finance can run a reimbursement to you once we have a corrected EOB showing the adjustment. Email finance-ops@redwood.com.

olivia.p: Thanks everyone. Will post updates. If insurer stalls, happy for benefits to escalate to our carrier rep. Appreciated :relieved:
